newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking pulls down Bombay stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pulls down Bombay stocks at close.

text.p: Share prices closed with small losses at Bombay bourses on Monday, after a bout of profit-taking capped price gains, dealers said.
"There was some profit-taking, but market action was more or less flat," said Balaji Narayan, dealer at Prime Broking, a domestic firm.
"Volumes were pretty decent.. not much of fund activity."
Dealers said operators' reluctance to keep long positions in a shortened trading week led to the squaring up mood, dealers said.
"Nobody's willing to take up fresh positions..a small correction was also long overdue," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokerage firm Pashupati Advani.

The market rallied 229.93 points, or nearly 8.0 percent in the last six sessions on fresh political developments in the Congress party. The party is to elect a new chief of its parliamentary bloc after former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao quit last week.

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and most other bourses close for Christmas holidays from Wednesday. The BSE re-opens on January 1, but the National Stock Exchange trades on Thursday, closes on Friday and re-opens on December 31.
The BSE's 30-share index fell 18.30 points, or 0.59 percent, to close at 3,091.89, off 3,127.19, an intra-day high. The 50-stock index of the NSE lost 3.43 points, or 0.39 percent, to end at 880.95.
SBI fell 2.75 rupees to 225.25, Reliance 3.25 to 201.75, TISCO 2.75 to 163.0, BSES 3.0 to 207.50, TELCO 2.75 to 339.0, Bajaj Auto 3.50 to 840.0 and Indian Hotels 19.0 to 711.25.
However, ACC gained 5.50 to 1,190.25, ITC 6.25 to 303.0, MTNL 2.75 to 238.0 and Colgate 7.50 to 235.0.
